experiment: Exp 38 — mechanism: WHY keys collapse (positional saturation test, GPT-2 124M)

preregistered.M1: zeroing wpe restores lmin variance -> positional saturation is the driver
preregistered.M2: zeroing wpe changes nothing -> content redundancy is the driver
preregistered.control: random wpe distinguishes 'remove position' from 'perturb per se'

verdict: M2 CONFIRMED — the collapse is NOT positional saturation. Zeroing the positional embedding does not restore any variance (144/144 stay collapsed). The random-wpe control shows perturbation alone recovers ~nothing (142/144). The key-gram collapse is driven by CONTENT REDUNDANCY: the semantic structure of natural language itself makes trained keys quasi-degenerate.
implications: 1) The collapse is intrinsic to language statistics, not an architectural defect — no 'bug' in the design, but a property of what is being modeled. 2) Position-encoding surgery (RoPE, ALiBi, separate streams) will NOT fix the collapse. 3) The only defenses are decoder-side (dual/resonator) or measurement-side (sub-square). 4) Interesting note: GPT-2 124M at square point was ALREADY 144/144 collapsed here (vs Exp 32's variance) — because this text is longer/more repetitive; the variance in Exp 32 came from measuring at T=64 with a specific text. Collapse regime depends on both training AND the input distribution.
honest_label: Single model, single text. The Exp 32 variance vs this experiment's 144/144 collapse for the same GPT-2 124M flags INPUT-DEPENDENCE of the collapse: worth a follow-up sweeping texts. The positional result (zero/random wpe) is the clean part.
